instruction: I'm having difficulty tracking my mouse cursor on the screen. Please make the cursor larger so I can see it more easily.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

result.command: CURSOR_SIZE=$(timeout 10 gsettings get org.gnome.desktop.interface cursor-size 2>/dev/null | grep -oE "[0-9]+" | head -1); if [ -n "$CURSOR_SIZE" ] && [ "$CURSOR_SIZE" -gt 24 ]; then echo "Large cursor enabled (size: $CURSOR_SIZE)"; else echo "Default cursor size"; fi

metadata.explanation: Task requires increasing cursor size via Settings > Accessibility > Cursor Size. Evaluator checks if cursor-size > 24 pixels (default is 24). Uses existing check_include_exclude metric with vm_command_line getter.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly queries GNOME cursor-size setting via gsettings command
Logic properly verifies cursor size > 24 (default value), matching instruction requirement to make cursor larger
check_include_exclude metric correctly distinguishes success (includes 'Large cursor enabled') from failure (excludes 'Default cursor size' and 'error')
Complete coverage: instruction requires larger cursor, evaluator verifies size increase
Robust edge case handling: timeout protection, stderr suppression, empty string check, numeric extraction
No UI state dependency: reads persistent system setting, no postconfig needed
Command execution is feasible and reliable using standard GNOME utilities
